title: Approximate satisfaction after coin-tape conversion
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$, with inputs in $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$. Let $Q:X\to Y\to\alpha\to\mathrm{Prop}$ be a predicate, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\delta>0$. If, for every $x,y$, the probability that $p$ fails to satisfy $Q(x,y,\cdot)$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then the protocol obtained by converting $p$ to a coin-tape protocol with slack $\delta$ has failure probability at most $\varepsilon+\delta$ for every $x,y$.
hypotheses_covered: A public-coin finite-message protocol $p$ over $\Omega$, with inputs $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
For every input pair, $p$ has failure probability at most $\varepsilon$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over a finite probability space
$\Omega$, with private input sets $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$; let $Q : X \to Y
\to \alpha \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be a predicate; and let $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ be real
numbers with $\delta > 0$. If $p$ approximately satisfies $Q$ with error at most
$\varepsilon$, then the coin-tape protocol obtained by converting $p$ with slack
$\delta$ approximately satisfies $Q$ with error at most $\varepsilon + \delta$.
